# MongoDB query built from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/nosql-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-943](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/943.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in a MongoDB query, on a collection of the MongoDB Node.js driver or a Mongoose
model (Express, Fastify, Next.js):

- as the whole filter, or as a field value of a filter (also inside `$or`, `$and` and `$nor`, and
  in Mongoose's `where()`), where it can carry query operators;
- inside `$where`, `$function` or `$accumulator`, where it runs as JavaScript on the database.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Express's JSON parser, and its query-string parser in Express 4, turn request data into objects. A
client who sends `{"password": {"$ne": null}}` instead of a string turns "the password equals this
value" into "the password is anything", which can bypass a login or return other users' data. In
`$where` a value can run JavaScript on the database server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the customer value from the JSON body is used as it is.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { MongoClient } = require('mongodb');

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
const client = new MongoClient(process.env.MONGO_URL);
const orders = client.db('shop').collection('orders');

app.post('/orders/search', async (req, res) => {
  const found = await orders.find({ customer: req.body.customer }).toArray();
  res.json(found);
});
```

**Compliant:** the value is converted to a string, so it cannot carry operators.

```javascript
const express = require('express');
const { MongoClient } = require('mongodb');

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
const client = new MongoClient(process.env.MONGO_URL);
const orders = client.db('shop').collection('orders');

app.post('/orders/search', async (req, res) => {
  const found = await orders.find({ customer: String(req.body.customer) }).toArray();
  res.json(found);
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Convert each value to the type you expect: `String(x)`, `Number(x)`, or a validated schema.
- Or compare explicitly: `{ customer: { $eq: x } }`, so an object stays a value.
- With Mongoose, use `sanitizeFilter` (`mongoose.set('sanitizeFilter', true)` or per query).
- Never build `$where`, `$function` or `$accumulator` code from request data.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- MongoDB Node.js driver
- Mongoose

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Query values from Express 5's and Fastify's default query parsers are strings, but they are
  still reported.
- A `typeof x === 'string'` check before the query is not recognised.
- `String()` also counts as safe inside `$where` text, so `$where: "..." + String(x)` is missed.
- Fastify body schemas are not read: a route with a literal `schema.body` option is left out of
  operator checks, whatever its types.
- A field value is followed when it is a variable or a property chain (`req.body.email`); other
  expressions such as `(await request.json()).author` are not.
- Collections are recognised by `db.collection(name)` in the same file, and Mongoose models by
  `mongoose.model(...)` in the same file or an import from a `models` path. After
  `mongoose.set('sanitizeFilter', true)` the whole file is taken as safe, also for driver
  collections.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
- Handlers that destructure the request are followed (`({ query }, res) => ...`,
  `const { body: { name } } = req;`), except a field with a default value in the parameter list
  (`({ query = {} }, res)`), which is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
